Understanding Sciatica: Causes and Symptoms Understanding Sciatica and Its Symptoms Sciatica is characterized by pain that travels along the sciatic nerve, which runs from the lower back through the hips and buttocks, down each leg. Symptoms can vary but commonly include leg pain, numbness, tingling, and weakness in the affected leg. The discomfort can be sharp or debilitating, often exacerbating with movement or sitting for extended periods. Several health issues can lead to sciatica, with herniated discs being one of the most prevalent causes. According to recent data, approximately 40% of individuals experience sciatica at some point in their lives . Another common condition is spinal stenosis, where the spinal canal narrows, putting pressure on nerves. Piriformis syndrome can also trigger symptoms by compressing the sciatic nerve. Recognizing these conditions early can help in managing sciatica effectively. When to Seek Professional Help If you experience persistent pain or worsening symptoms, it's crucial to consult a healthcare professional. Early evaluation can lead to quicker recovery. Techniques for Effective Treatment of Sciatica Core Strengthening Exercises Building core strength is essential for relieving sciatica . A strong core supports the spine, reduces strain on the lower back, and can alleviate pressure on the sciatic nerve. One effective exercise is the bridging exercise . Here’s how to do it: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Press your feet into the floor as you lift your hips towards the ceiling. Hold for a few seconds, squeezing your glutes at the top. Lower back down slowly. For beginners, start with 5-10 repetitions and gradually increase as your strength improves. Modifications, such as lifting one leg while holding the bridge, can challenge more advanced practitioners. Stretching Techniques for Relief Incorporating stretches into your routine can dramatically enhance flexibility and reduce tension around the sciatic nerve. The piriformis stretch is particularly beneficial: Lie on your back and cross one leg over the other, placing the ankle on the opposite knee. Carefully grab the thigh of the lower leg and gently pull towards your chest. Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in the glutes and outer hip. This stretch can be done daily, but it's important to listen to your body. Overstretching may cause more pain; if discomfort arises, ease off the stretch. title: AALAS 2024 highlights: Trends powering the next era of in vivo studies
summary: Three trends stood out as high priority for every lab at AALAS 2024: an eagerness to collaborate with scientific colleagues outside of in vivo teams, a desire to digitize lab processes, and an openness to engaging AI.
body_text: In vivo research practices are adapting quickly, with digitization allowing the rapid collection of a lot more data and shaping the way we study different therapeutic areas. This is reflected in the increased adoption of cloud-based solutions. According to Benchling’s 2nd annual State of Tech in Biopharma Report , 23% of small and 17% of large biopharma have adopted cloud-based scientific software or SaaS. For the first time at the 75th American Association of Lab Animal Sciences Congress (AALAS) 2024, AI was a prominent theme on the agenda. Throughout sessions and conversations with industry innovators, three trends stood out as high priority for every lab: an eagerness to collaborate with scientific colleagues outside of in vivo teams, a desire to digitize lab processes, and an openness to engaging AI and integrate SaaS solutions/instruments to maintain the best animal welfare practices. 1. Eliminate silos of data and errors One area that was highlighted frequently was how to use technology to prevent data collection errors for in vivo researchers. Relatedly, innovators isolate their teams if they become siloed from the upstream and downstream teams with whom they collaborate on a daily basis. Specifically, technology needs to connect scientists to prevent task duplication and data silos. If teams can’t directly share data and get a holistic view across teams, they put a lot at risk: This can lead to study repeats and an inability to gain any insight when comparing experiments. Benchling In Vivo enables better collaboration for scientists across the R&D lifecycle, allowing teams to spend more time on science and less on repetitive manual tasks. 2. Digitize lab processes — no more paper! Many scientists and technicians discussed how they’re digitizing lab processes to overcome data repeatability issues and speed up manual processes. This requires digital tools that can connect parts of the vivarium while maintaining the highest levels of 3Rs compliance (Reducing, Refining and Replacing animals in scientific discovery). Animal studies often involve a component run externally through a CRO (e.g. assays on animal samples or the entire study itself). Data from the CRO often comes in PDF/Excel/Word or powerpoint, requiring a time-intensive and error-prone process of restructuring such that it can be aggregated and graphed. Capturing, organizing, and analyzing study data is a challenge for many scientists. It’s also hard to capture data in a structured and objective way — especially when there are multiple scientists collaborating on a data set. Labs are looking to remove manual data entry, which leads to human errors and adds unnecessary steps into a process where time is critical. Benchling In Vivo task and enhanced device connectivity which allows for automated data capture and reduced human error and lab time. Investigating the use of LLMs to ingest CRO data in a structured format, preventing errors. From the bench to your inbox Our monthly newsletter features science insights, industry best practices, and stories from teams pushing biotech forward. 3. Build the highest level of animal welfare practices into lab workflows Many scientists expressed that lab technology’s lack of interoperability is a challenge. There are tools and softwares for animal breeding and reporting, animal identification, data capture, in-life measurement, sample handling, and more. Some of these are now taking advantage of AI to automate laborious tasks. While each one aims to individually improve the speed, consistency, and accuracy of the scientific process, it’s only truly efficient when those tools integrate seamlessly together. In fact, having too many disconnected tools can slow your team down, impacting animal welfare. Unifying tech used in the vivarium makes it possible to uphold the highest levels of 3Rs compliance. Benchling has continued to build integrations with partner organizations (a.tune and softmouse) for activities like colony management to support regulatory reporting, animal identification (UID and RapID) to improve tracking during studies, and analytics packages to gain insights of trends between studies (Prism). All of these help to improve staff morale, while maintaining best practices for humane animal management. Powering in vivo innovation From embracing the power of AI, to improving collaboration while keeping the highest standards of animal welfare, the AALAS community has again proved its dedication to innovate. Benchling is committed to the same goals, and we are looking forward to continuing these conversations with our European colleagues at FELASA 2025 in Athens (June), and to doing it all again at AALAS 2025 in Long Beach! title: Pros / Cons of Loop Timers vs. Camera timers
summary: As drive-thru technology advances, QSR operators face a choice: stick with traditional loop timers or adopt modern, AI-powered camera timers. While loop timers have provided basic timing data for yea…
body_text: As drive-thru technology advances, QSR operators face a choice: stick with traditional loop timers or adopt modern, AI-powered camera timers. While loop timers have provided basic timing data for years, camera timers offer a far more comprehensive and adaptable solution for today’s fast-paced environment. For operators aiming to elevate efficiency and customer experience, camera timers stand out as a game-changer. How Camera Timers Transform Drive-Thru Management Camera timers go beyond merely tracking vehicle presence and wait times. Leveraging AI technology, they deliver real-time insights that allow QSR managers to optimize operations with precision and depth that loop timers simply cannot match. Key Advantages of Camera Timers Real-Time Visibility and Data Depth: Camera timers provide continuous, detailed monitoring of drive-thru lanes, capturing not just timing but vehicle position, order point delays, and bottleneck locations. This allows managers to adjust staffing or service flow on the fly, reducing overall wait times and improving customer satisfaction. Advanced Analytics and Insights: Beyond immediate visibility, AI-powered camera systems generate comprehensive data that can reveal patterns in customer behavior, peak times, and traffic flow. These insights empower managers to make strategic decisions on staffing, promotions, and even menu design based on real-world data. Scalability and Centralized Control: For multi-unit operators, camera timers allow centralized control over numerous locations. This enables regional managers to view metrics across locations, helping them benchmark performance and implement improvements chain-wide. Why Loop Timers Can Fall Short in Today’s QSR Landscape While loop timers may be sufficient for basic vehicle tracking, they lack the versatility and depth of insight needed for a comprehensive operational strategy. Limitations of Loop Timers Basic Data Collection: Loop timers offer only simple entry-and-exit timestamps. They cannot capture granular data on where cars might be stalled in the line or identify common pain points in the process, limiting opportunities for targeted improvements. No Remote Access or Visual Feedback: Without visual or remote access, loop timers leave managers in the dark about real-time conditions. This can be a setback for larger franchises where remote monitoring would streamline management. Outdated Technology for Evolving Needs: As the QSR industry continues to prioritize data-driven improvements, relying on loop timers alone may limit growth. They do not integrate with analytics platforms, nor do they support AI, leaving operators without tools to adapt quickly. Why Camera Timers Are the Future for QSRs For operators looking to stay competitive in a demanding market, camera timers represent a strategic investment in the future. Their ability to capture and interpret complex data gives QSR operators the edge they need to exceed customer expectations and refine operations proactively. Enhanced Customer Experience: With camera timers, managers can promptly address delays and adjust staffing or processes in real-time, delivering a smoother, faster drive-thru experience. Data-Driven Decision Making: AI-powered analytics offer insights into customer behavior, service speed, and peak times. This enables QSR operators to make informed, data-backed decisions on promotions, staffing, and process changes. Improved Accountability and Security: Camera timers add a layer of security to the drive-thru, recording any anomalies or incidents. For operators concerned about loss prevention or operational accountability, this visual record proves invaluable. While loop timers have served the QSR industry reliably, the modern drive-thru demands more. Camera timers, with their AI-driven insights and real-time adaptability, offer an unmatched solution for QSRs committed to maximizing operational efficiency and customer satisfaction. For operators ready to embrace advanced technology, camera timers provide the insight, control, and scalability needed to thrive in an increasingly competitive landscape.

title: E-Lojistik Nedir? Avantajları Neler?
summary: Lojistik nedir diye düşünenler için, ürün ve hizmetlerin üretim aşamasından tüketim noktasına kadar transferinin planlanması, uygulanması ve yönetilmesi olarak ifade edilebilir. E-ticaret lojistiği ile geleneksel lojistik arasındaki farkları keşfedin ve işletmenize sunduğu verimlilik avantajlarını öğrenin.
body_text: E-Lojistik Nedir? Avantajları Neler? Kamion » Lojistik Terimler Sözlüğü » E-Lojistik Nedir? Avantajları Neler? Yazar : Kamion Lojistik 15 Kasım 2024 - Lojistik Terimler Sözlüğü Loading... 2193 Görüntülenme Lojistik nedir diye düşünenler için, ürün ve hizmetlerin üretim aşamasından tüketim noktasına kadar transferinin planlanması, uygulanması ve yönetilmesi olarak ifade edilebilir. E-lojistik ise geleneksel lojistik süreçlerinin dijital teknoloji ile entegre edilmesidir. Özellikle e-ticaretin hızla yaygınlaşmasıyla, lojistik sektöründe yeni bir bakış açısı doğmuştur. Pandemi döneminde e-ticaretin yüksek ivme kazanmasıyla e-lojistik kavramı daha çok ön plana çıkmıştır. Geleneksel lojistik süreçlerinden farklı olarak, e-lojistik dijital platformlar ve otomasyonlar kullanılarak yönetilir. Bu yönetim biçimi, taşımacılık faaliyetlerinin daha hızlı, çevik ve etkin olmasını sağlar. E-lojistik, ürünlerin dijital ortamlarda sipariş edilmesinden, depolanmasına, taşınmasına ve müşterilere teslim edilmesine kadar olan tüm süreçleri kapsar. E-lojistik, sadece malların fiziksel taşınması değil, aynı zamanda bu süreçlerin izlenmesi, optimize edilmesi ve dijital sistemlerle kontrol edilmesi anlamına gelir. RFID, barkod sistemleri, veri analizleri ve otomatik yönetim sistemleri gibi teknolojiler, e-lojistik süreçlerinde büyük rol oynar. Özellikle envanter kontrolü, sipariş yönetimi ve rota planlaması gibi kritik alanlarda bu teknolojiler kullanılır. Teknolojinin lojistik süreçlerine dahil edilmesi, işletmelere hız, maliyet tasarrufu ve daha iyi müşteri hizmetleri avantajı kazandırır. İçindekiler Toggle E-Lojistik Faaliyetleri Nelerdir? E-lojistik, taşımacılık faaliyetlerine dijital teknolojilerin entegre edilmesiyle oluşur ve çeşitli süreçleri kapsar. Bu süreçler, siparişlerin alınmasından depolama ve taşıma işlemlerine kadar geniş bir yelpazede yer alır. Geleneksel lojistikten farklı olarak, e-lojistik faaliyetlerinde otomasyon ve veri analitiği kullanımı ön plandadır. Gelin, e-lojistik faaliyetlerini yakından inceleyelim. Sipariş Alma E-lojistikte siparişler dijital platformlar üzerinden alınır ve otomatik sistemlerle işlenir. Pandemi döneminde tüm dünyada yaşanan e-ticaret patlaması, tüketicilerin alışveriş alışkanlıklarını büyük oranda değiştirmiştir. Sipariş alma süreci, müşteri memnuniyeti açısından kritik bir öneme sahiptir. Çünkü siparişlerin doğru ve hızlı bir şekilde alınması, sevk edilmesi gereken ürünlerin tespitini kolaylaştırır. Üstelik satın alma davranışını kolay hale getirmek, müşterilerin memnuniyeti açısından önemlidir. Envanter Kontrolü Depo Yönetim Sistemleri ve RFID teknolojileri, stokların sürekli olarak izlenmesini sağlar. Bu sayede ürünlerin eksik ya da fazla stoklanması gibi sorunlar ortadan kalkar. Lojistik süreçlerin hızlanması ve depolama maliyetlerinin azalması için envanter kontrolünün dijital şekilde yapılması önemlidir. Taşıma ve Dağıtım Taşıma ve dağıtım süreçleri, taşıma yönetim sistemleri aracılığıyla planlanır. Bu sistemler, siparişlerin en uygun rotalarla, minimum maliyetle ve çevresel sürdürülebilirlik ilkesine uygun şekilde taşınmasını sağlar. Rotasyonun güncel veriler ışığında planlanması, lojistik süreçlerinin verimli şekilde ilerlemesi için önemlidir. Yakıt maliyetlerinden tasarruf etmek, müşteri memnuniyetini sağlamak ve çevreye duyarlı bir taşımacılık faaliyeti gerçekleştirmek için rotasyonun doğru planlanması gerekir. Veri Analizi ve Otomasyon E-lojistik süreçleri büyük veri analitiği ile desteklenir. Siparişler, envanter ve dağıtım süreçlerinde toplanan veriler analiz edilerek, lojistik operasyonları daha verimli hale getirilir. Bu analizler sayesinde işletmeler, daha doğru kararlar alarak operasyonlarını yönetebilirler. Otomasyon kullanımı, işgücü maliyetlerini azaltır ve insan kaynaklı hataları minimum seviyeye indirir. Geleceğin lojistik dünyasında başarılı olmak isteyen şirketler, teknolojik sistemlere yatırım yapmalıdır. Müşteri yolculuğunun haritalandırılması ve verilerin doğru kullanılması, artık ticarette şirketlerin başarısını etkileyen en önemli unsurların başında gelmektedir. E-Lojistik ile Geleneksel Lojistik Arasındaki Farklar Nelerdir? Geleneksel lojistik ile e-lojistik farkı; dijitalleşme olarak karşımıza çıkar. E-lojistik, tamamen dijital platformlar üzerinden yürütülürken, geleneksel lojistik manuel işlemlerle gerçekleştirilir. Örneğin, e-lojistik kavramında envanter kontrolü, sipariş takibi ve taşıma süreçleri dijital sistemlerle yönetilir. Geleneksel lojistikte ise bu süreçler manuel yapıldığı için fazla zaman alır ve insan kaynaklı hatalara daha açıktır. E-lojistikte, tüm taşımacılık süreçleri anlık olarak izlenebilir. Siparişin hangi aşamada olduğu, ne zaman teslim edileceği gibi bilgiler dijital platformlar üzerinden takip edilebilir. Geleneksel lojistikte ise bu izlenebilirlik daha sınırlıdır​. Lojistik dünyasında bilgi, başarıyı belirleyen en temel unsurlardan biridir. Uçtan uca görünürlük, lojistik sektöründe rekabet avantajı sağlar. E-lojistik; rota optimizasyonu, yakıt tasarrufu ve daha az karbon salınımı gibi çevresel faydalar sunar. Özellikle dijital rota planlama ve veri analizi sayesinde taşıma süreçleri çevreye duyarlı şekilde yönetilebilir. Sürdürülebilirlik kavramı, yeni tüketici profilinde önemli bir etkiye sahiptir. Müşteri memnuniyeti sağlamak ve daha yaşanabilir bir dünya için çalışmak, şirketlerin hedefleri arasında yer alır. E-lojistik sistemleri, şirketlerin sürdürülebilirlik hedeflerine ulaşmasını kolaylaştırır. E-Lojistiğin Avantajları Nelerdir? E-lojistik, işletmelere ve müşterilere birçok avantaj sağlar. Dijitalleşme ve otomasyon teknolojileri sayesinde işletmeler hem maliyet avantajı elde eder hem de süreçlerini hızlandırır. E-lojistiğin sunduğu avantajları detaylı şekilde inceleyelim. Verimlilik Artışı: Dijital çözümler ve otomasyon sistemleri, lojistik süreçlerinin hızlanmasını sağlar. Veri analitiği ve otomasyon sayesinde manuel işlemler ortadan kalkar. Dijital sistemler ile yapılan operasyonlarda insan kaynaklı hatalar azalır ve süreç daha hızlı ilerler. Hızlı ve İzlenebilir Teslimat: E-lojistikte siparişlerin dijital olarak takip edilebilmesi ve teslimat süreçlerinin otomasyonlarla yönetilmesi, çevik bir yaklaşım sunar. Müşterilere hızlı teslimat yapılabilmesi için lojistik süreçlerinin dijitalleştirilmesi önemlidir. Uçtan uca görünürlük sağlayan e-lojistik faaliyetleri, müşterilerin siparişlerini her aşamada izleyebilmesini mümkün kılar. Stok Yönetimi ve Envanter Kontrolü: Dijital sistemlerle entegre stok yönetimi, envanterin gerçek zamanlı olarak izlenmesini sağlar. Fazla veya az ürün bulundurma riski azaldığı için stok maliyetleri düşer. Depolama maliyetleri azalır ve lojistik süreçleri daha az maliyetle yönetilebilir. Maliyet Tasarrufu: Rota planlaması ve taşıma yönetimi sistemleri sayesinde yakıt maliyetleri etkili şekilde hesaplanabilir. Lojistik süreçlerde iş gücünün azalması ve otomasyonların devreye girmesi, işçilik maliyetlerinden de tasarruf edilmesini sağlar. İletişim ve İşbirliği Kolaylığı: E-lojistik; tedarikçiler, taşıyıcılar ve müşteriler arasında daha güçlü bir iletişim kurulmasına yardımcı olur. Elektronik Veri Değişimi ve Müşteri İlişkileri Yönetimi gibi dijital çözümler, lojistik süreçlerdeki verimliliği artırır​. Uçtan uca görünürlük ve gerçek zamanlı veriler sayesinde bilgi anında tüm taşımacılık paydaşlarına aktarılır. Beklenmeyen durumlarda hızlı aksiyon alınması için iletişimin sürekli olması önemlidir. E-Lojistik ve Tedarik Zinciri Yönetimi E-lojistik, tedarik zinciri yönetiminde büyük bir dönüşüm sağlar. Tedarik zincirinin etkili şekilde yönetilmesi, ürünlerin doğru zamanda, doğru yerde olmasını gerektirir. Veri analitiği ve otomasyon sayesinde, tedarik zincirindeki süreçler izlenebilir hale gelir. Tedarik zincirindeki tüm paydaşlar dijital platformlar üzerinden süreci takip ederek işbirliği içinde çalışır. Geleceğin ticaret dünyasında başarılı olmak isteyen şirketler, tedarik zinciri yönetimindeki teknolojik gelişmeleri yakından takip etmelidir. E-Lojistik Yaparken Dikkat Edilmesi Gerekenler E-lojistik süreçlerinde başarı elde edebilmek için dijital altyapının doğru bir şekilde kurulması ve yönetilmesi gerekir. E-lojistik faaliyetlerini uygularken dikkat edilmesi gereken unsurları iyi bilmek ve hassasiyet göstermek önemlidir. Üzerinde durulması gereken önemli noktaları beraber değerlendirelim. E-lojistik yaparken işletmelerin ilk olarak güvenilir ve profesyonel bir bilgi teknolojileri altyapısına sahip olması gerekir. Bu altyapı, tüm lojistik süreçlerin dijitalleşmesine olanak tanır ve manuel iş süreçlerini ortadan kaldırarak operasyonları hızlandırır. Ancak böyle bir altyapıya sahip olmak, başlangıç maliyeti gerektirir. Teknolojik altyapısı güçlü lojistik partnerler ile çalışmak, şirketleri yüksek maliyetlere katlanmaktan kurtarır. Kamion gibi dijital uygulamalar, e-lojistik süreçlerinde kritik bir rol oynar. Kamion, araç takip sistemleri, rota planlaması, envanter yönetimi ve taşıma optimizasyonu gibi birçok e-lojistik sürecini tek bir platformda yönetmeyi sağlar. Ayrıca, tedarikçilerle, taşıyıcılarla ve müşterilerle olan işbirliğini de güçlendirir. E-lojistik süreçlerinde, büyük veri analitiği ile işletmeler siparişlerden, stok yönetimine, teslimat süreçlerinden müşteri memnuniyetine kadar geniş bir yelpazede bilgi toplar. Bu verilerin analizi sayesinde etkili ve verimli kararlar alınabilir. Veri analitiği, hangi ürünlerin daha çok talep gördüğünü, hangi bölgelerde daha hızlı teslimat yapılabileceğini ve stokların nasıl optimize edilebileceğini anlamaya yardımcı olur. Burada dikkat edilmesi gereken en önemli nokta, verilerin doğru analiz edilmesidir. Bilgi ve becerisi yüksek kişilerin e-lojistik sektörüne kazandırılması verilerin doğru analiz edilmesinde önemli rol oynar. E-lojistik süreçlerinin dijitalleşmesi, aynı zamanda siber güvenlik risklerini de beraberinde getirir. Lojistik süreçlerde kullanılan dijital sistemler, hacker saldırıları, veri sızıntıları ve siber tehditler gibi risklere açık hale gelir. İşletmelerin dijital altyapılarını korumak için güçlü siber güvenlik çözümleri uygulamaları önemlidir. E-lojistik süreçlerinde başarılı olmak için; profesyonel bir IT altyapısının kurulması, otomasyon çözümlerinin taşımacılık süreçlerine etkili şekilde entegre edilmesi ve siber güvenlik önlemlerinin alınması gereklidir. Şirketler e-lojistik faaliyetlerini uygulamak için yüksek başlangıç maliyetlerine katlanmak istemiyorsa, teknolojik altyapısı güçlü partnerler ile çalışabilir. Yük bulma uygulaması , e-lojistik süreçlerinin etkili şekilde uygulanmasını sağlar. Yük arayanlar ve yük verenler arasında hızlı bir iletişim sağlayan Kamion, lojistik sektörüne yeni bir soluk kazandırmakta. title: NEW JERSEY NATURAL GAS ENCOURAGES CUSTOMERS TO TAKE PRECAUTIONS AND GUARD AGAINST POTENTIAL SCAMS ON UTILITY SCAM AWARENESS DAY
body_text: New Jersey Natural Gas NEW JERSEY NATURAL GAS ENCOURAGES CUSTOMERS TO TAKE PRECAUTIONS AND GUARD AGAINST POTENTIAL SCAMS ON UTILITY SCAM AWARENESS DAY 11/14/2024 - For Immediate Release November 14, 2024 – New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG), principal subsidiary of New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR), is joining with Utilities United Against Scams to raise awareness and encourage customers to guard against impostors posing as utility representatives. November 20th is Utility Scam Awareness Day, an important reminder for utility customers to stay vigilant and recognize the signs of potential utility scams. By better understanding these signs, NJNG customers can protect themselves from scams and take proper steps if they notice suspicious activity. “New Jersey Natural Gas encourages our customers to be familiar with common red flags of utility scams so they can safeguard their sensitive personal and financial information,” said Marissa Travaline, vice president of Customer Service, Marketing and Energy Efficiency. “Never trust anyone who pressures you for immediate payment or makes any unusual utility request. Customers should always contact their utility provider to confirm that any outreach is legitimate.” Unsuspecting utility customers are targeted by impostors acting as utility representatives. Some examples of the strategies scammers use include: Falsifying caller ID and sending phishing emails that appear to be from NJNG. Emails from NJNG are sent from @njng.com or @4you.njng.com. Threatening to turn off services (via phone or in-person) unless immediate payment is made via prepaid credit card, Venmo®, Apple Pay®, etc. NJNG only accepts online payments via its online customer portal. “Slamming” scams that switch customers to another energy supplier without their authorization. Customers are encouraged to use caution when sharing their NJNG account numbers and fully evaluate and understand any offer of service before agreeing. Tricking customers into thinking they are eligible for a credit card. NJNG does not offer credit cards. If a customer receives a call, an email or unexpected visit from someone claiming to be an NJNG representative, they should verify the source by contacting the company at 800-221-0051 or CustomerCare@njng.com. Alternately, NJNG’s contact information can be found on the customer’s natural gas bill and company website. When NJNG representatives come to the door, they carry official company photo ID and drive commercial vehicles clearly marked with the NJNG logo. If a customer is in arrears, NJNG communicates through written notices via mail or through attempts to work with them to find payment solutions. NJNG employees will never demand immediate payment or request banking and personal information. To learn more ways to stay safe against scams, visit njng.com/safety and the Federal Trade Commission’s website at consumer.ftc.gov/scams . About New Jersey Resources New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a Fortune 1000 company that, through its subsidiaries, provides safe and reliable natural gas and clean energy services, including transportation, distribution, asset management and home services. NJR is composed of five primary businesses: New Jersey Natural Gas , NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve approximately 582,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean and parts of Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties. Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects with a total capacity of approximately 474 megawatts, providing residential and commercial customers with low-carbon solutions. Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America. title: The Ultimate Guide to Preparing for Interview Questions|Coprehensive Interview Prep
summary: Discover essential strategies and tips in 'The Ultimate Guide to Preparing for Interview Questions.' Master different types of interview questions, including behavioral, technical, and situational. Optimize your interview prep with expert advice and effective practice methods. Ideal resource for anyone looking to ace their next job interview
body_text: The Ultimate Guide to Preparing for Interview Questions Introduction to Interview Prep Questions To feel confident and prepared for an interview: research the company, practice common questions, prepare for behavioral questions, have questions to ask the interviewer, be well-rested, well-dressed, and have necessary documents ready. interview prep questions can make a big difference. Knowing what to expect can help build confidence, ease nerves, and boost performance during those critical moments. Many candidates often overlook this vital step, believing that being knowledgeable about job-related topics suffices. However, understanding common interview prep questions transforms an interview from a daunting task into an exciting opportunity. When approaching interview prep questions, start by reflecting on past experiences. Think about achievements, challenges, and how you overcame obstacles. These personal stories often resonate well, allowing interviewers to connect with your background and skills. Consider structuring responses using popular formats like STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result). This method provides clarity and keeps answers focused. Research plays a crucial role too. Familiarize yourself with industry-specific interview prep questions. Different roles may have distinct requirements, so tailoring practice responses can significantly enhance preparedness. Utilize online forums, professional networks, or company review sites to discover insights from others who have gone through similar interviews. Their experiences can be invaluable. Mock interviews can also be incredibly helpful. Practicing responses with a friend, mentor, or career coach allows for real-time feedback and helps refine delivery style. This practice not only improves answers but also reduces anxiety, creating a more relaxed atmosphere when facing real interviewers. Finally, remember that interview prep questions often focus on both technical skills and cultural fit. Companies seek candidates who align with their values and contribute positively to team dynamics. Therefore, consider how personal attributes and experiences align with company missions and objectives. The right preparation can turn a stressful experience into a seamless process. Embracing interview prep questions ensures candidates present authenticity, professionalism, and clarity, setting a solid foundation for success. Understanding Different Types of Interview Questions Preparing effectively for interviews involves understanding various types of interview prep questions. Each category serves a purpose and helps interviewers gauge different aspects of a candidate’s suitability. Familiarizing yourself with these can enhance confidence and improve performance on interview day. Behavioral questions often focus on past experiences, asking candidates to recall situations where they demonstrated skills or overcame challenges. Examples might include inquiries like, "Describe a time when you had to work under pressure." Responding well requires using the STAR method—Situation, Task, Action, Result—allowing candidates to narrate compelling stories showcasing their abilities. Situational questions present hypothetical scenarios, prompting candidates to explain how they'd handle certain challenges. For instance, “What would you do if a team member missed a deadline?” This type of question assesses problem-solving skills and creativity, offering interviewers insight into thought processes and decision-making. Technical questions delve into industry-specific knowledge or skills. These are crucial for roles requiring specialized expertise. Candidates might encounter queries like, “Can you explain how you approach coding in Java?” Preparing for these types of questions ensures familiarity with relevant concepts, making it easier to respond confidently. Cultural fit questions explore alignment between a candidate’s values and the company culture. Questions such as, “What type of work environment do you thrive in?” help interviewers understand whether a candidate would integrate well with existing teams. Candidates should reflect on personal values and how they connect to the company's mission. Finally, general questions serve as openers, inviting candidates to share their stories. Typical questions may include, “Tell me about yourself.” Although they seem straightforward, these questions provide opportunities to highlight relevant experiences, skills, and motivations. In summary, a thorough understanding of different question types enhances interview prep. Candidates who recognize behavioral, situational, technical, cultural fit, and general questions can tailor responses accordingly. This targeted preparation boosts chances of impressing interviewers and landing desired positions. Top Behavioral Interview Questions and How to Answer Them Behavioral interview questions can feel challenging, but preparing well can boost confidence and improve responses. These questions often start with phrases like "Tell me about a time..." or "Give an example of..." They're designed to assess past behavior as a predictor of future performance. One common question involves teamwork: "Describe a time when you worked successfully as part of a team." To answer effectively, provide a specific example. Start by outlining the situation, explaining your role, and detailing actions taken. Finally, share the outcome, emphasizing how collaboration led to success. Another frequent inquiry focuses on challenges: "Tell me about a difficult situation and how you handled it." Choose a situation that showcases resilience and problem-solving skills. Detail obstacles faced, actions taken to overcome challenges, and lessons learned, demonstrating growth. Employers often ask about conflict resolution: "Explain a time when you disagreed with a colleague." In this instance, discuss the disagreement respectfully, outline steps taken to address it, and highlight a positive resolution or compromise. This shows ability to manage conflict professionally. Adaptability also ranks high among interview prep questions. A typical query might read: "Share an experience where you had to adapt to change." Describe your initial thoughts about the change, how you adjusted, and what positive results followed. This illustrates flexibility and willingness to embrace new situations. Finally, employers appreciate seeing initiative: "Give an example of a time you took on a leadership role." Discuss a specific project or situation where you stepped up, describing actions taken and outcomes achieved. Highlight how this experience shaped personal development and growth. Preparation is crucial for successfully navigating these types of questions. Practicing with friends, using mock interviews, or even writing down responses can help. Focus on clarity, keeping responses concise yet informative. By understanding these common queries and practicing thoughtful answers, candidates can approach interviews equipped for success, transforming anxiety into confidence. Common Technical Interview Questions and Strategies Preparing for technical interviews can feel overwhelming, but breaking down common questions helps ease anxiety. Understanding what interviewers seek makes a big difference during conversations. Here are some frequently asked technical interview questions and strategies for tackling them. First, a popular question revolves around algorithms and data structures. Interviewers often ask candidates to solve problems on the spot. Brush up on key concepts, including sorting algorithms, linked lists, and trees. Practicing coding challenges on platforms like LeetCode or HackerRank can sharpen skills and boost confidence. Another common inquiry involves system design. Candidates may be asked to design a scalable application or database. When addressing such questions, focus on demonstrating your thought process. Discuss trade-offs, scalability, and potential bottlenecks. Sketching diagrams can help clarify ideas and showcase your approach. Behavioral questions, although not technical, often pop up in interviews. For instance, interviewers might ask about past projects or challenges faced. Use the STAR method—Situation, Task, Action, Result—to structure responses. This technique allows you to highlight relevant experiences while keeping answers focused. Additionally, some interviews include practical coding tests or pair programming sessions. In these scenarios, communication plays a vital role. Explain your thought process clearly as you write code. This transparency not only demonstrates technical understanding but also shows collaboration skills, which are crucial in team environments. Lastly, mock interviews can prepare you for real-life scenarios. Practicing with friends, mentors, or through online platforms gives insight into different styles of questioning. Encourage constructive feedback to refine your approach. Overall, becoming familiar with common technical interview questions prepares you for success. By honing skills and practicing responses, you build confidence, turning potential stress into manageable challenges. Focus on continuous learning, and remember each interview serves as a valuable experience, no matter the outcome. Preparing for Situational Interview Questions When tackling situational interview questions, a thoughtful approach can really set candidates apart. These questions often start with phrases like, "Tell me about a time when..." or "Describe a situation where..." Crafting compelling responses requires reflection and preparation. First, it’s essential to understand what employers look for. They want insight into how past experiences demonstrate problem-solving skills, decision-making abilities, and a capacity to handle stress. Preparing answers ahead of time can create a solid foundation for showcasing unique abilities. One effective strategy involves using the STAR method. This stands for Situation, Task, Action, and Result. Begin by briefly describing a relevant situation from past experiences. Follow up with the task at hand, detailing what needed addressing. Next, focus on actions taken to tackle that situation. Finally, wrap up by sharing results achieved, highlighting positive outcomes or lessons learned. This structured technique provides a clear narrative, helping hiring managers grasp thought processes. Practice makes perfect. Role-playing with a friend or using mirror exercises can enhance confidence. Try recording answers too, allowing candidates to review and refine responses. Listening to recordings offers an opportunity to identify strengths and areas needing improvement. Another key aspect involves tailoring answers to align with company culture and job role specifics. Research beforehand helps understand values and expectations of potential employers. Thus, responses can be adjusted to reflect what truly matters to them. Lastly, stay calm and composed during interviews. Remember, conversation flows both ways. Consider situational questions as chances to showcase personality alongside qualifications, turning nervous energy into enthusiasm. Revisiting common interview prep questions will also aid candidates in feeling more comfortable. Reviewing scenarios and practicing responses can make a significant difference in overall performance. Embrace preparation as a chance to shine, revealing not just qualifications but also genuine passion for roles pursued. Confidence and clarity can leave lasting impressions, setting candidates up for success in potential new journeys. Tips for Practicing Interview Questions Effectively Preparing for interview questions can feel overwhelming, but practicing effectively makes a world of difference. Start with a solid set of interview prep questions that reflect common themes in your field. Prioritize those that align with specific job expectations. Begin by writing down answers. Focus on clarity and conciseness. Use bullet points to outline key points, making sure to highlight achievements and relevant experiences. This ensures preparation remains focused on what matters most. Next, practice aloud. This helps build confidence and allows for adjustments in tone and pacing. Consider recording oneself; reviewing this footage offers great insight into body language and speaking habits. Keep an eye on fidgeting or nervous gestures to improve overall delivery. Involve a friend or mentor. Conduct mock interviews, using those prepared questions. Constructive feedback from a trusted individual can help identify strengths and areas for improvement. Plus, hearing questions from another perspective simulates real interview scenarios. Time your responses. Many interviewers appreciate succinct answers, often preferring responses within two minutes. This keeps conversations engaging and demonstrates respect for time. Utilize resources like online platforms or interview coaching services. Many offer practice questions and even simulations, enhancing preparation experiences. Lastly, focus on self-care before interviews. Ensuring adequate rest and nutrition aids concentration and reduces anxiety. Remember, consistent practice makes perfect. Review progress regularly, refining answers based on feedback. Embrace each opportunity as a learning experience. With dedication and thoughtful preparation, confidence grows, leading to greater success during those important interviews. Resources for Interview Question Preparation When diving into interview prep questions, having the right resources can make a significant difference. Various tools and materials exist to help candidates feel confident and ready for any challenge. One essential resource includes websites dedicated to job-seeking. Sites like Glassdoor and Indeed offer insights into common interview questions based on specific job roles and industries. Browsing through these platforms provides a clear understanding of what to expect during an interview, along with real experiences shared by other candidates. Books on interview strategies also play a crucial part in preparation. Titles such as "Cracking the Coding Interview" focus on tech-related questions, while "The Complete Job Interview Handbook" covers a wider array of industries. These books often outline various interview prep questions, along with tips on answering effectively. Online courses can also enhance preparation. Platforms like Coursera and Udemy offer interview preparation courses, often featuring video tutorials and practice exercises. This interactive approach allows candidates to engage with material actively, boosting confidence. Additionally, these courses may include mock interviews where learners can practice answering typical interview prep questions in a supportive environment. Podcasts dedicated to career advice can provide valuable insights too. Many industry experts share their experiences and advice, helping listeners understand what interviewers look for in responses. Personal stories combined with professional recommendations can illuminate effective strategies for tackling interview questions. Networking serves as another great resource. Connecting with professionals in desired industries can yield tips and advice that feel relevant and personalized. Joining professional groups on LinkedIn or attending industry meetups opens opportunities to gain insights from those who’ve successfully navigated interviews. Practicing with a friend or mentor can provide immediate feedback. Role-playing different scenarios allows candidates to refine responses and improve overall delivery. Utilizing multiple resources not only prepares individuals for common interview prep questions but also builds self-assurance, leading to a more successful interview experience. title: Cost Management Strategies for Real Estate Owners: Navigating Rising Construction Expenses and Interest Rates
summary: In today’s volatile market, real estate asset owners face the dual challenge of rising construction costs and high interest rates, both of which impact profitability and long-term value. For owners managing capital-intensive projects, controlling expenses without sacrificing quality is more critical than ever. This article explores practical cost management strategies specifically for real estate owners who seek to balance financial pressures with the demand for durable, high-value assets. By adopting innovative approaches to material procurement, workforce efficiency, and project scheduling, real estate asset owners can better control costs on the margins and protect their investments.
body_text: 1. Optimizing Material Costs Through Strategic Procurement Material costs make up a substantial part of project expenses, and recent supply chain disruptions have exacerbated pricing volatility. To mitigate these effects, asset owners are increasingly using strategies that focus on timing, supplier relationships, and bulk purchasing. Bulk Purchasing and Supplier Partnerships : Forming long-term relationships with suppliers can yield volume discounts and priority access to materials. By committing to multi-project or long-term agreements, real estate owners can often negotiate better prices and hedge against future price increases. Flexible Procurement Timing : Monitoring market conditions and purchasing materials during periods of lower demand can help reduce costs. Some asset owners are now working with procurement teams to adjust schedules and purchase materials in advance when prices are more favorable. Alternative Materials and Substitutions : As certain materials become cost-prohibitive, exploring alternatives can offer savings. For instance, opting for high-quality recycled materials or sustainable options can reduce initial outlays without compromising structural integrity or longevity. By combining these strategies, real estate owners can mitigate the impact of rising material costs while maintaining quality. 2. Implementing Value Engineering Without Compromising Quality Value engineering (VE) is a technique used to maximize the value of a project by improving function and reducing costs. When applied thoughtfully, VE helps owners make data-driven choices about where to allocate resources for the best return. Functionality-Driven Decisions : Rather than reducing costs across the board, value engineering involves identifying where the project can achieve functional goals with fewer resources. For example, instead of using high-cost custom fixtures, real estate owners might select readily available alternatives that still offer the desired aesthetic and durability. Lifecycle Cost Analysis : Evaluating materials and systems based on their full lifecycle cost, rather than only upfront expenses, can often reveal opportunities to cut costs in the long term. Opting for durable materials with lower maintenance needs, even if initially more expensive, may reduce repair and replacement costs down the line. Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration : When teams from different disciplines, such as architecture, engineering, and construction, collaborate early in the planning process, they can identify efficiencies in the design phase. This approach reduces costly redesigns later on. Value engineering, when strategically implemented, allows asset owners to control costs and ensure long-term quality and functionality. 3. Utilizing Technology for Greater Cost Control Technology is a powerful tool in modern project management, enabling owners to optimize processes, track spending, and reduce waste. Leveraging tech solutions not only enhances visibility but also streamlines management, leading to more efficient use of capital. Project Management Software : Tools that integrate budgeting, scheduling, and resource allocation provide real-time visibility into project finances and timelines. By centralizing data, project managers can quickly identify cost overruns and adjust resources as needed. Real-time tracking also allows for early identification of potential delays, enabling proactive solutions that reduce expensive downtime. Building Information Modeling (BIM) : BIM platforms enable detailed virtual modeling, making it easier to visualize and plan complex projects. By simulating the construction process, owners and contractors can identify potential issues early, reducing the likelihood of expensive rework or design changes. BIM also facilitates better coordination among stakeholders, which can further reduce project costs. Drones and On-Site Monitoring : Drones and remote monitoring technologies allow for efficient site assessments and progress tracking, minimizing the need for on-site personnel and reducing inspection times. These tools help identify inefficiencies, monitor safety compliance, and track progress, all of which contribute to better cost control. Using these technologies can streamline operations, reduce administrative overhead, and keep projects on schedule and within budget. 4. Improving Labor Efficiency Through Workforce Optimization Labor shortages and high wage demands have driven up construction labor costs in recent years. To manage these expenses, real estate owners are implementing workforce optimization strategies to enhance productivity without increasing headcount. Enhanced Training Programs : Skilled labor is not only more efficient but also less likely to make costly mistakes. By investing in targeted training, asset owners can reduce rework and improve productivity. Training programs that focus on new construction techniques and technology use also create a workforce that is adaptable to changes in project requirements. Staggered Scheduling : Adjusting work schedules to accommodate peak productivity times can improve efficiency. For instance, during certain phases of a project, working longer hours on fewer days can minimize downtime. By carefully timing labor allocation, owners can reduce labor costs without compromising project quality. Cross-Training Staff : Multi-skilled workers can perform a wider range of tasks, reducing the need for specialized labor and streamlining staffing needs. Cross-training programs allow workers to fill multiple roles, enabling more flexibility in scheduling and reducing potential bottlenecks. Workforce optimization strategies like these can maximize the productivity of available labor and offset the impact of rising wage costs. 5. Mitigating Interest Rate Impact Through Financial Planning High interest rates increase borrowing costs, which directly affects the profitability of capital projects. To minimize these costs, real estate owners are adopting proactive financial strategies. Fixed-Rate Financing Options : Locking in fixed rates, especially during periods when interest rates are expected to rise, provides cost certainty and simplifies long-term financial planning. Fixed-rate loans protect owners from rate fluctuations, allowing them to plan expenses with greater accuracy. Staggered Financing Models : Instead of financing an entire project upfront, some owners use staggered financing or phased lending. By only borrowing funds as needed, they reduce immediate interest expenses and free up cash flow for other project areas. Capital Reserves and Cash Flow Management : Maintaining a reserve fund can provide a buffer against interest rate increases, reducing the need for high-interest emergency funding. Effective cash flow management also ensures that funds are available for critical project phases, reducing reliance on borrowing during construction. These financial planning strategies help reduce exposure to high interest rates and ensure a more predictable financing environment. 6. Sustainable Building Practices for Long-Term Savings Sustainable construction can be a cost-effective way to manage long-term expenses, and green building strategies often reduce operational costs even if they require a larger initial investment. As utility costs rise, energy-efficient designs become particularly valuable. Energy-Efficient Systems : Installing energy-efficient HVAC, lighting, and water systems can substantially reduce operating costs. Over time, these systems pay for themselves in the form of lower utility bills, providing an ongoing cost-saving benefit for real estate owners. Sustainable Material Choices : Using locally sourced or recycled materials can reduce transportation costs, while materials with longer lifespans and low maintenance requirements can lower future CapEx outlays. Tax Incentives and Grants : Many governments offer incentives for green building practices, such as tax credits or grants. Leveraging these can offset initial costs, making sustainable construction financially viable while reducing long-term expenses. Sustainable practices offer a dual benefit: they reduce environmental impact while controlling operational costs for asset owners. 7. Enhanced Project Scheduling for Cost Efficiency Proper scheduling is essential for minimizing costs, as delays can significantly increase expenses. Strategic scheduling practices allow real estate owners to control costs related to both labor and materials. Critical Path Analysis : By identifying and focusing on critical tasks that directly impact the project timeline, owners can allocate resources more effectively. This approach minimizes downtime, keeps the project moving smoothly, and reduces the risk of budget overruns. Just-in-Time Delivery : Scheduling material deliveries to align closely with project needs reduces storage costs and minimizes material waste. This approach requires careful coordination but can lower expenses significantly by reducing on-site material handling and inventory requirements. Contingency Planning : Building contingency plans into the schedule helps manage unexpected delays. Having alternative plans or buffer periods reduces the financial impact of unforeseen issues, keeping the project on track and on budget. These scheduling techniques allow for more precise control over project timelines and reduce the risk of costly delays. Conclusion As construction costs increase and interest rates remain high, real estate asset owners need innovative strategies to protect their investments and maximize returns. By focusing on material optimization, value engineering, technology adoption, workforce efficiency, proactive financial planning, sustainable practices, and precise scheduling, asset owners can better navigate today's economic pressures. These strategies not only address immediate challenges but also lay the groundwork for long-term operational savings and enhanced asset value. By implementing these practical solutions, real estate owners and project managers can optimize their capital spending, stay within budget, and deliver projects that are financially and operationally sound, despite a challenging economic environment.

title: Beyond Barcodes: The Rise of BLE in Asset Tracking
summary: Explore the impact of EU battery regulations on compliance and sustainability, and how Energous' wireless power solutions enable a battery-free future.
body_text: When it comes to logistics, the efficient tracking and management of assets and inventory are critical. For years, Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) has been the go-to solution. However, as technology evolves and scalability becomes a more pressing concern, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is emerging as a more cost-effective and versatile alternative. Understanding the key differences between these technologies can help businesses decide which one is the best solution for their operational needs. Understanding RFID RFID has been widely adopted in supply chain and logistics industries for tracking assets, inventory, and goods in transit. RFID systems use radio waves to read information stored on tags attached to items. An RFID reader can scan these tags at various distances, depending on the type of RFID system (passive, active, or semi-passive). However, this out-of-date technology – which has been around since the 1940s – comes with significant drawbacks: – High Equipment Costs: RFID readers typically cost between $1,500 and $3,000, which makes large-scale deployment expensive. The average warehouse for a medium-sized business is about 40,000 square feet, meaning you would need to spend more than $65k on 30 RFID readers for adequate coverage. – Proprietary Systems: RFID systems generally operate within their own proprietary setups, meaning they are often incompatible with other systems or technologies like smartphones, tablets, or Bluetooth-enabled devices. – Limited Flexibility: Because RFID readers and tags work within a closed system, integrating RFID requires costly hardware, software, and infrastructure changes. – Planned Obsolescence: RFID systems require periodic upgrades, with companies typically needing to replace and/or upgrade their RFID readers every few years. This planned obsolescence increases long-term costs and operational disruptions. What is BLE, and How Does It Work? BLE (or Bluetooth Low Energy) is a wireless communication technology that has become ubiquitous across many industries due to its low power consumption, ease of integration, and compatibility with everyday smart devices – and it is now gaining traction for smart supply chain applications. BLE is a subset of the Bluetooth standard, designed specifically for applications that require low energy usage, such as asset tracking tags, smart home systems, and IoT devices. BLE readers, such as smartphones, tablets, or dedicated BLE gateways, detect and receive signals from nearby BLE tags or beacons. These tags periodically broadcast small packets of data, such as location or sensor information, which the readers pick up. The readers then relay this data to a central system for processing, allowing for real-time tracking and monitoring of assets or environmental conditions. BLE technology offers several advantages that are helping drive its adoption as a replacement for traditional RFID solutions in asset tracking: – Cost-Effectiveness: BLE requires a much less expensive infrastructure compared to RFID. Many businesses already use BLE-enabled devices like smartphones, tablets, and computers, which can easily communicate with BLE tags or sensors. Businesses can further reduce costs by using battery-less BLE devices, which eliminate the need for frequent battery replacements and maintenance. These devices are energized via a wireless power network (WPN) which enables them to be continuously charged in place. This not only cuts down on operational interruptions but also lowers long-term maintenance costs. The simplicity of the BLE devices combined with the efficiency of a WPN enables businesses to create truly autonomous, low-maintenance IoT systems at a fraction of the cost of traditional RFID or battery-dependent BLE solutions. – Scalability: BLE’s open standard allows for easier scalability. Unlike RFID, which often necessitates specialized hardware, BLE can integrate with existing infrastructure, making it ideal for businesses looking to expand operations without massive upfront investments. – Widespread Compatibility: One of BLE’s biggest strengths is its compatibility with a wide range of modern devices. Almost every smartphone, tablet, and computer supports Bluetooth, meaning BLE can be accessed without additional hardware purchases. – Real-Time Data: BLE enables real-time tracking of assets, just like RFID, but its flexibility in integration means that companies can access the data through common platforms like smartphones or tablets without needing proprietary readers. With the latest innovations in wireless power solutions , data streams at the edge are always active, providing 24/7 tracking. Furthermore, BLE technology offers high level of visibility and process automation reducing to almost zero any type of human intervention. RFID vs. BLE: Head-to-Head Comparison While both RFID and BLE are used for asset tracking, the following factors highlight why BLE is becoming a more popular choice: Transforming Asset Tracking with Battery-free BLE While BLE is already having an impact on how companies track their assets, Energous Wireless Power Solutions is enabling the technology to deliver even greater visibility, control, and automation. Energous PowerBridge transmitter systems use RF waves to deliver wireless power to devices while simultaneously enabling real-time data communication over BLE. They are the backbone of WPNs that allow devices such as sensors and tags to continuously provide critical enterprise data to cloud networks—at distance and without wires, batteries, or cables—ensuring they are reliably charged at all times. In addition, they act as data links, enabling the devices to efficiently communicate valuable data and insights back to the cloud, and allowing companies to analyze, optimize, and improve every part of their supply chain operations in real time. title: Public vs. Private Real Estate: Key Differences
summary: LPL Research examines public and private real estate markets, cap rate divergence, and why REITs may offer attractive value today.
body_text: Assessing Public vs. Private Real Estate Dynamics Michael McClain | Alternative Investment Research Analyst and Due Diligence Last Updated: August 05, 2026 Public vs. Private Real Estate While real estate is often treated as a single asset class, investors access it through two distinct markets: public real estate, primarily via publicly traded Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), and private real estate, through direct ownership or private funds. Both convey an ownership interest in the underlying properties, but they differ in pricing mechanism, liquidity, and valuation practice. REITs trade continuously, so valuations adjust in real time to economic data, rate expectations, and earnings. Private real estate relies on periodic appraisals and infrequent transactions. As a result, public markets often lead private markets both into and out of dislocations. Current Market Dynamics The cleanest way to see this is through capitalization (cap) rates, which represent the unlevered yield on a property, calculated as net operating income (NOI) divided by value. Cap rates move inversely to price: a higher cap rate implies a lower valuation. Historically, the spread between REIT implied cap rates and private appraisal cap rates has been modestly positive. Today's gap sits well outside the normal range. As of the first quarter of 2026, the REIT implied cap rate was 5.89% versus an NCREIF ODCE1 private appraisal cap rate of 4.44%, a spread of 145 basis points, and the 17th consecutive quarter of divergence. Since the fourth quarter of 2021, the 10-year Treasury yield has risen 267 basis points, while REIT implied cap rates responded, increasing 144 basis points from 4.45% to 5.89%. Private appraisal cap rates moved just 58 basis points, to 4.44%, essentially the level at which public REITs were priced at the end of 2021. While cap rates between the two markets are not expected to match due to reporting lags, differences in sector composition, and liquidity characteristics, they would typically be expected to move in the same direction, particularly following a meaningful increase in the 10-year Treasury yield. One reason these gaps can persist is that public and private investors process information differently. REIT investors continuously incorporate changes in interest rates, financing conditions, leasing trends, and economic expectations into security prices. Private market participants, by contrast, often focus on long-term property cash flows and rely on appraisal-based valuation methodologies that update less frequently. During periods of rapid market change, this can make public real estate appear excessively pessimistic or optimistic relative to private valuations. Historically, however, public pricing has often served as an early indicator of the direction private market values ultimately take as transactions and appraisals gradually reflect evolving market conditions. LPL Research Takeaway If spreads narrow toward longer-term levels, convergence is likely to occur through a combination of REIT price appreciation, increasing private-market cap rates, and improving transaction activity. Under most convergence scenarios, public REITs appear better positioned on a risk-adjusted basis given their liquidity, transparency, and current valuations. Private real estate is by no means expected to face widespread declines, rather expectations are for private market cap rates to adjust upward, especially as the 10-year Treasury yield has moved materially higher. Also, while the lagged private valuations remain rich for assets with strong NOI growth, in higher-demand sectors, these valuations can be supported as investors are willing to accept a lower current yield in exchange for higher future cash-flow growth. For investors, a tighter level in cap rates would likely coincide with greater price transparency and transaction volume, ideally helping create a stronger base level to build off. Overall, we believe real estate may have a place in diversified portfolios as part of a broader real assets sleeve, with a preference for sectors supported by long-term structural demand. 1 NCREIF ODCE (officially the NCREIF Fund Index – Open-End Diversified Core Equity, or NFI-ODCE) is a benchmark that measures the investment performance of open-end, core real estate funds that primarily own diversified, stabilized U.S. commercial properties. It is a capitalization-weighted, time-weighted index reported gross of fees and is widely used by institutional investors to track the performance of core private real estate.
